payload.headline: Micron drops 13.89% to 594.51, breaking support; call moves from hold to wait

summary.thesis: Micron is a grade A business on a trailing P/E of 8.0, but its 74.59% operating margin is at a 5-year peak, and the price now assumes cash flow will shrink.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy only at the 471.0 support. Swing: no trade before the 2026-12-17 report.
summary.act_at: buy at 471.0; return to hold on a close above 658.73

payload.happening: MU fell 13.89% in one day to 594.51, from 690.44. It closed below yesterday's 643.69 support floor, and that old support zone (now 643.27–658.73) has become resistance. None of the news in DATA explains the drop, and the next earnings report is on 2026-12-17.
payload.business: Nothing in DATA shows the business changed today. The latest quarter ended 2026-09-03 and was filed 2026-10-09. It showed trailing revenue of 133.2B, up from 37.4B, and free cash flow of 59.0B, up from 1.7B. The gross margin was 80.72% and the operating margin 74.59%, up from 26.14%. The balance sheet is not at risk: Micron has 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt, so its net cash is 40.6B. Share dilution is small at 1.78% a year. The main business risk is the margin. The filings say the 75% operating margin sits at the top of a 5-year range that runs from -41% to 75%, and peaks like that usually fade. Memory is a cyclical business where prices swing with supply and demand (general knowledge). Today's 13.89% fall changes the price and the mood, not the reported numbers. It can still be a sign that the market expects the margin to fade before the 2026-12-17 report shows it. DATA has no segment breakdown and no analyst estimates, so demand by end market cannot be checked here.

worth.text: No discounted cash flow (DCF) value is given. A DCF values a company on its future cash, but free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year, and a jump like that can't simply be projected forward. Two other methods are left. First, the stock's own history: at its usual 5-year price-to-sales levels, the share is worth 322.32 (low), 490.66 (middle) or 833.11 (high). Second, a cash-flow sketch with a 10.1% discount rate: if free cash flow just holds flat, the share is worth 706.64. The price of 594.51 implies free cash flow starting to shrink by 4.4% a year. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption: does today's peak margin last? The own-history method assumes it returns to normal. The cash-flow method assumes it mostly holds. If the operating margin falls to 37% with 20% starting growth, the value is 783.05, but that case needs the growth to show up. One quirk: the valuation summary in DATA still quotes yesterday's 690.44 price. My fair-value range runs from the own-history middle, 490.66, to the zero-growth value, 706.64.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near 59.0B instead of shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin fades from the top of its 5-year range.

bull: The trailing P/E is 8.0 and price-to-sales is 5.1, below the peer median of 8.2. The growth-adjusted ratio against peers is 0.28.
If free cash flow just holds flat, the share is worth 706.64, above the 594.51 price. The price already assumes cash flow shrinking by 4.4% a year.
Net cash of 40.6B and 59.0B of trailing free cash flow give the company room to get through a downturn.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin is at the top of its 5-year range and up from 26.14%, and the filings say peaks like this usually fade.
The trend is down. The price is below the 20-day (786.65), 50-day (912.19) and 200-day (772.36) averages, with the 20-day and 50-day still falling.
The own-history middle value is 490.66, below the price. Options traders hold 1.94 puts for every call.

levels.what: Top of the 435.76–471.0 support zone, which has held 5 times. It is close to the 490.66 own-history middle value. This is the level to buy.
Top of the 643.27–658.73 zone, which was support and is now resistance. A close above it would show the break was a false signal and would move the call back to hold.
Bottom of the strongest support zone. A close below it would move the call to avoid until the 2026-12-17 report shows where margins are heading.

longterm.why: The stock broke the 643.69 floor that yesterday's note set as the trigger to move from hold to wait. At 594.51 it sits inside the 490.66–706.64 fair-value range with no margin of safety while the trend is down.

swing.why: The trend is down, and resistance at 643.27 is less than one ATR (average daily price range, 61.83) above the price. The nearest support, at 471.0, is far below, so a trade has little upside for its risk. There is no trade until the price either holds at the 435.76–471.0 support or closes above 658.73.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-17 report falls one day before the 2026-12-18 options expiry, which prices a 17.6% move. Any position taken before the report carries that event risk, and the operating margin it shows will decide between the 490.66 and 706.64 ends of the range.

change_mind: A close above 658.73 takes back the broken support zone. That would move the long-term call back to hold.
A 2026-12-17 report with the operating margin still near 74.59% while the price sits near 471.0 would turn wait into buy.
A close below 435.76, or a reported operating margin below 37% (the level where the value falls to 783.05 even with 20% starting growth), would turn wait into avoid.
payload.what_changed: Changed: the 594.51 close broke below the 643.69 support floor that yesterday's note named as the trigger, so the long-term call moves from hold to wait, and the next report date in DATA is now 2026-12-17 instead of 2026-12-23.
